docstring:
If $n(n+1)=2^k3^lm$, where $(m,6)=1$, then is it true that
$\limsup_{n\to \infty} \frac{2^k3^l}{n\log n}=\infty$?
references: [Er76d] Erdős, P, Problems and results on number theoretic properties of consecutive integers and related questions. Proceedings of the Fifth Manitoba Conference on Numerical Mathematics (Univ. Manitoba, Winnipeg, Man., 1975) (1976), 25-44.
type_pretty: True ↔ Filter.limsup (fun n => ↑↑(2 ^ Erdos933.k n * 3 ^ Erdos933.l n) / (↑↑n * ↑(Real.log ↑n))) Filter.atTop = ⊤
